recent.text: After combining for 78 against Indiana, Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving scored 22 on 9-of-23 shooting at Minnesota. “They had one body on them before they even crossed half-court,” Mavericks coach Dusty May said. Read more on @DALSportsJrnl: https://t.co/8bjjS5Kncc

recent.text: Minnesota scored 74 points in the paint and made all 10 of its second-chance field goals against the Mavericks. “Coach put a very good game plan together for us, and I think we let that slip,” Naji Marshall said. Read more on @DALSportsJrnl: https://t.co/TCjPmLPbGy

recent.text: Zaccharie Risacher had 21 points over his previous five games. He scored 22 off the Mavericks’ bench at Target Center on 9-of-14 shooting. “A reflection of the work I’m putting every day,” Risacher said. Read more on @DALSportsJrnl: https://t.co/bOvUMAplf0

recent.text: Dallas pulled within 43-42 in the second quarter. Minnesota outscored the Mavericks 60-27 through the third. “The most disappointing, just the way we responded to the runs,” Mavericks coach Dusty May said. Read more on @DALSportsJrnl: https://t.co/FxPg32pULz

recent.text: Minnesota’s top-ranked defense held the Mavericks to 0.703 points per half-court possession in a 133-94 win at Target Center. “We kind of settled for somewhat good ones,” Mavericks coach Dusty May said. Read more on @DALSportsJrnl: https://t.co/27JKZIvGeZ
